title: Safai Saathi adoption record
description: Who has caught up with which change. Each app updates its own record in its own repo, in .contract/adopted.json. This file is the platform's aggregated view. It is a REPORT, not a source of truth. The truth is each app's own file.

x-rules.sourceOfTruth: Each app's own .contract/adopted.json in its own repo. This file is generated from those files and this repo's manifest. An app with no file shows contractVersion null and adoptionFile null, and its statuses are derived from the manifest, never carried as evidence.
x-rules.noChecklistNoProgress: An app with no checklist shows 0 percent, not 100 percent.
x-rules.evidenceRequired: A status of adopted needs a merged PR as evidence. The CI tool checks it.
x-rules.notApplicable: A status of not_applicable needs a note saying why.
x-rules.generatedBy: Generated by 08-tools/sync-adoption.ts from each app's .contract/adopted.json and this repo's manifest. Do not hand-edit the statuses.

checklist.task: Call flagMockLocation({ tripId }) from the tracking engine where the direct trip write was
Latch locally after the call succeeds, as today
Retry the call on reconnect if it failed offline
Never send detected: false and never try to clear the latch

CHG-0017.note: The engine keeps the local latch for the banner and persists it through the callable. A failed call retries on the regular GPS cadence, so a reconnect lands it without another mocked fix. No client trip write is attempted.

checklist.task: Write notices/{noticeId}/receipts/{driverCode} with readAt when the driver opens a notice
Take the receipt doc id from the driverId claim
Keep the session-local unread set as the fallback until the write path works
Compute the dot from the cached receipts plus the local set
Do not add a receipt array to the notice document

CHG-0018.note: The flow writes readAt through the server clock and reads the receipt back per visible notice, because the strict rules authorize a receipt by its doc id and a collection-group query cannot be authorized that way. A denied read or write, which is what the loose PHASE 1 rules do, falls back to the session-local set; the dot clears for the session and no notice is hidden.

CHG-0020.note: The admin panel is the only affected app. The driver app never writes the driver document and its own driver read stays field-restricted; it never reads these audit fields.
